abstract_sentences.text: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), with their event-driven and biologically inspired mechanisms, are well-suited for energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware.
Neural coding, which is critical to SNNs, determines how information is represented via spikes.
abstract_sentences.link: narrows from SNNs to neural coding

evidence.anchor: Neural coding, which is critical to SNNs

abstract_sentences.text: While Time-to-First-Spike (TTFS) coding uses a single spike per neuron to offer extreme sparsity and energy efficiency, it often suffers from unstable training and low accuracy due to its sparse firing.
abstract_sentences.comparison: TTFS benefits versus its sparse-firing training cost
abstract_sentences.link: creates the gap addressed in sentence 4

evidence.anchor: often suffers from unstable training and low accuracy

abstract_sentences.text: To address these challenges, we propose a training framework that incorporates parameter initialization, training normalization, a temporal output decoder, and a re-evaluation of the pooling layer.
abstract_sentences.link: introduces four components developed in sentences 5--7

evidence.anchor: we propose a training framework that incorporates

abstract_sentences.text: The proposed parameter initialization and training normalization mitigate signal diminishing and gradient vanishing, which helps stabilize training.

evidence.anchor: mitigate signal diminishing and gradient vanishing

abstract_sentences.text: Our output decoder aggregates temporal spikes to encourage earlier firing, thereby reducing latency.

evidence.anchor: encourage earlier firing, thereby reducing latency

abstract_sentences.text: The re-evaluation of the pooling layer demonstrates that max-pooling violates single-spike constraints, which should be avoided, whereas average-pooling preserves them.
abstract_sentences.comparison: max-pooling versus average-pooling under one-spike constraints

abstract_sentences.text: Experiments show that our framework stabilizes and accelerates training, reduces latency, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy for step-by-step TTFS SNNs on MNIST (99.48%), Fashion-MNIST (92.90%), CIFAR10 (90.56%), CIFAR100 (70.27%) and DVS Gesture (95.83%).

evidence.anchor: achieves state-of-the-art accuracy for step-by-step TTFS SNNs

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper links causal TTFS instability to time-averaged Kaiming variance, subsequent weight drift, non-differentiable first-spike decoding, and pooling’s one-spike condition; ETTFS-init, normalization, TWD, and average pooling answer those links (p.4--p.6, §§4.2--4.5).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: It keeps the overview, Eqs. (1)--(29), main benchmark tables, latency/energy estimates, and component/gradient/depth/gamma ablations in p.1--p.9.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: It moves T/variance sensitivity, rate-coding comparison, exact architectures, and hardware/reproducibility statements to p.12--p.13; robustness and architecture reproduction depend on those pages.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 previews distribution/convergence/latency, then Eqs. (15)->(16) and (26)->(27) tie local mechanisms to design choices before Table 4 recombines components (p.2, p.5--p.6, p.9).
final_judgment.largest_gap: Benchmark and energy claims are conditioned by heterogeneous models/pre-training/implementations, undefined ± values, unstated seed/training protocol, and estimates rather than deployed hardware measurement (p.7--p.8).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a decomposable system claim, pair each design choice with a local invariant or derivation and with an explicitly comparable ablation/result object.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: A local derivation and an engineering estimate cannot by themselves establish a general performance or deployment claim when randomness, external baselines, hardware, or data scale dominate.
